title: Bound Tauri backend HTTP requests by total deadline
summary: Enforce one monotonic total deadline across Tauri loopback backend connect, request write, and response read operations.
reason: Remediate P2 AUDIT-FIND-W09-005. Per-operation socket timeouts could be reset forever by a loopback peer that made slow incremental progress.
behavior_before: Backend requests used two-second connect/read/write timeouts independently and read until EOF, allowing a peer that sent one byte before each read timeout to keep synchronous lifecycle calls blocked forever.
behavior_after: Backend requests share a five-second monotonic deadline across connect, all request writes, and all response reads while retaining the two-second per-I/O ceiling and 16 MiB response cap.
tests_added: A loopback server drips response bytes faster than the socket timeout and is still rejected by an injected short total deadline.
The Tauri scaffold requires the five-second total budget, deadline-aware capped reader, and shared deadline argument.

notes: This changes only loopback shell transport availability and does not alter backend command semantics or media policy. No media is read or mutated, so representative real-media validation is not required.
